title: World War One Adventure
welcome_lead: It's 1914. Europe is sliding into the Great War. Climb into the trenches and meet the soldiers of WW1. 🎖️
meta_desc: WW1 Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of the First World War, the trenches and the Western Front.
final_note: You met the MAIN causes of WW1, life in the trenches, and the Armistice on 11 November 1918.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Before 1914, Europe was split into two big groups of allies.

The four long-term causes are remembered as MAIN: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism.

The trigger came in June 1914: a Serbian shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary. Within weeks, the alliances pulled most of Europe into war. ⚔️

On the Western Front in France and Belgium, soldiers dug long lines of trenches.

Between them lay No Man's Land — barbed wire, shell holes and mud. Going 'over the top' meant facing machine guns.

Trenches were filled with rats, lice and rainwater. Diseases like 'trench foot' were common. Many soldiers suffered shell shock. 😢

Big battles included Verdun and the Somme in 1916. On the first day of the Somme, the British army lost about 57,000 men.

In 1917 the USA joined the war. In 1918 Germany ran out of soldiers and food.

The fighting stopped at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918 — the Armistice. We remember it every year on Remembrance Day. 🌺

mcqs.q: When did Nazi Germany move to a total war economy?
options: Only after Stalingrad in 1943, under Speer; before that Hitler had avoided full mobilisation to maintain civilian morale and consumer goods.
Germany never moved to a war economy because Hitler thought he would win quickly.
Germany was on a total war footing from 1939 onwards.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.
Britain restricted immigration because the Commonwealth ceased to exist in 1962.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
